notes: A real sign-in, and an honest account of what a lock on a downloadable file can and cannot do. The four shared access codes are replaced by your own email and password, checked against the database rather than against four hashes compiled into this page. Josh can now see every tablet that has signed in, and withdraw a person or a tablet centrally and instantly — no new file to build, no tablet to visit. Sign in once with signal and the app works with none at all for 30 days; past that it still opens, prints and exports every job already on the device, and one reconnection puts the rest back. It can never lock a mechanic out of a job he is standing in front of: the worst it will ever do is go read-only, and starting a new inspection and publishing are the only two things it stops. The grace window is counted by the server, so winding a tablet's clock back buys nothing. The four old codes keep working alongside the new sign-in until 31 October 2026, with a banner asking people to register.
validated_against: The FAA's own model search on drs.faa.gov, 23 models, Status=Current: 693 directives listed, 693 returned, 0 wrongly set aside. Perfect on every individual model. AD Toolbox's airframe lists hold 528 of the same 693 — mostly by design, since their appliance directives sit in a separate unmatched list of 581.
reliability: 188 self checks passing, 15 of them new and all about the lock: the offline grace boundary at day 29, day 31 and to the minute either side; a revoked tablet and a withdrawn person, both of which go read-only and never further; the four old codes during and after the transition; a clock wound backwards buying nothing; and a proof that no combination of server answer, date and stored code can produce any mode other than 'full' or 'readonly'. Six failure modes then driven end to end in a real browser — first run with no signal, day 29, day 31, revoked mid-job, signed in as the wrong shop, clock set backwards — 35 checks, 0 page errors. Database side: migration 014 with 49 isolation checks in 015, all passing, and migrations 002 and 005 re-run afterwards still at 7 and 15.

index.source: FAA Dynamic Regulatory System, AD Final Rules

storage: The directive index no longer shares a database with jobs and photographs. It lives in Cache Storage under 'adx-1'. Any copy left in the old place is deleted on first load. This is the second half of the 30 August fix: the database that wedged that morning is now smaller and is never touched by an AD search.
writer: The workbook is written by the app, not by a library. A stored zip and five XML parts, about 160 lines, so it works on a tablet in a hangar with no signal. Checked both ways: the file reads back byte-identical through the app's own reader, and opens clean in a strict spreadsheet parser.
language: Every British spelling and idiom taken out. "Aircraft" is now "aircraft" in all 86 places it appeared, and with it labour/labor, colour/color, authorisation/authorization, recognised/recognized, digitised/digitized, grey/gray, carburettor/carburetor, neighbour/neighbor, cancelled/canceled and the rest. Two idioms went with them: a "fortnight" is now a two-week window, and the legacy-directive note that told a mechanic which fortnight to look in now says which two-week issue. Nobody on a US ramp says aircraft.
